bib.title: Knowing When to Critique: Task-Adaptive Metacognitive Regulation for Reliable LLM Reasoning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Knowing When to Critique: Task-Adaptive Metacognitive Regulation for Reliable LLM Reasoning" (the MetaCrit framework). Xinmeng Hou*, Ziting Chang* (equal contribution; NTU), Zhouquan Lu (SJTU), Bohao Qu (A*STAR), Liang Wan and Wei Feng (Tianjin U), Hai Hu (CityU HK), Qing Guo (Nankai). Preprint, arXiv 2507.15015 v4 [cs.MA], dated 27 Sep 2026. The page-1 stamp is v4; the first submission was July 2025. The text says nothing about a venue (the format looks like ACL style). Code: github.com/Paparare/EduThink4AI. File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/08-eval/sources/hou-2025-knowing-when-critique.pdf

COVERAGE: All 144,576 chars and 39 pages were read, as 10 sequential chunks of the extracted text, plus the figure captions. Page 1 was covered by the first extraction preview. References were skimmed. Of the target note I read lines 1-344 of 524. I did not read the part after "Convergence in practice" (agent-specific suites, multi-turn, environment hygiene, checklist), but I grepped its headings and the rest of 08-eval for terms such as "self-refine", "metacog", "over-correct" and this paper's arXiv id.

IMPORTANT MISMATCH: scripts/papers/ledger.jsonl line 2164 files key 2507.15015 as "MCPEval" (status "downloaded", note 06-evaluating-agents.md, reason "Automates end-to-end agent evaluation over MCP"). The PDF is MetaCrit, not MCPEval. The ledger row has the wrong title and rationale. The PDF cannot support the reason given in the ledger. I did not verify what MCPEval's own arXiv id is.

FIT: This paper is not about evaluating agents. It is a prompting and orchestration method, and its evaluation is ordinary benchmark accuracy.
- 06-evaluating-agents.md: no good section. It has no trajectories, tool calls or environment state. At most it fits a one-line aside near the "Evaluate the components, then the whole" section or the efficiency/cost table, as a cost-per-correct data point. I would not file it there.
- 05-llm-as-judge.md "Known biases" (self-preference row) is the closest fit. The paper cites Xu et al. 2024 for self-bias in self-refinement. Its split (generate, then assess in a separate call) is the same reason given for judging with a different model. It supports one line only.
- 12-failure-modes.md could take the finding that unconditional critique over-corrects correct answers, as a caution for critique-then-revise graders or loops.
- 14-calibrating-judges... is about the judge's written critique, not critique-as-intervention. The fit is weak.
- The likeliest better home is outside 08-eval, in prompting or reasoning-loop notes (ai-engineering prompt-chaining/reasoning, generative-ai self-refinement). That is for you to decide.
- The note's existing "Cite even when covered" rule applies only if a note already covers raw-critique over-correction. I found none in 08-eval.

CORE CLAIM: Uniform critique hurts, and critique applied in proportion to need helps. MetaCrit runs four calls on every input: (1) a generator, (2) a read-only monitor that questions the answer's validity, (3) a controller that critiques, and (4) a synthesizer. "Adaptive" here means graded intervention strength inside a fixed pipeline. There is no gate and no stage skipping.

CLAIMS (ranked; all on GPT-3.5-Turbo unless stated; one run per cell, no seeds reported)
1. Appending a plain critique instruction degrades every baseline.
 number: Self-refine TruthfulQA 75.89 to 18.23 (-76.0%); MEP 89.35 to 27.66 (-69.0%).
 setup: "Distinguish trick questions if needed" appended to 8 baselines; TruthfulQA (n=817) and CIAR (n=50); GPT-3.5-Turbo. Table 1.
 quote: "Self-refine −76.0% on TruthfulQA, MEP −69.0%": critique embedded directly into the generation prompt "fires on every input without regard for whether the answer was already sound, and so over-corrects."
 where: p6-7, Table 1.
2. Headline accuracy.
 number: MetaCrit 94.12 TruthfulQA / 84 CIAR, against Zero-shot-CoT 70.38 / 24, MEP 89.35 / 82, o1 94.97 / 84.
 setup: TruthfulQA is judged by GPT-4o (Long et al. protocol). CIAR is human double-annotated. Table 1, Table 7.
 quote: "On the same GPT-3.5-Turbo backbone, MetaCrit reaches 94.12% and 84% (Table 1), matching dedicated reasoning models with a general-purpose one."
 where: p6.
3. Other structured monitor/control loops fall below plain Zero-shot-CoT.
 number: TruthfulQA/CIAR: Metacognitive Prompting 67.73/44, MGV 51.83/32, ReMA 52.32/32, SOFAI-LM 64.79/40.
 quote: "MGV, the most dynamic loop of the four (up to three difficulty-scaled re-monitor/re-generate cycles), performs worst, falling to 51.83 on TruthfulQA, eighteen points below Zero-shot-CoT's 70.38."
 where: p7.
 caveat: on GPT-4o these baselines are far more competitive (Table 9, 86.96 to 93.80 on several columns). The authors concede the margin is "largest exactly where regulation has work to do" (p15).
4. Significance is only established for TruthfulQA.
 number: MetaCrit 94.12 [92.3, 95.5] vs MEP 89.35, p<.001. CIAR 84 vs 82, n=50, p=.79. CREAK p=.35. CrowS-Pairs p=.15.
 quote: "the CIAR margin (84 vs. 82, n=50) is not [significant], so on CIAR MetaCrit matches rather than beats MEP."
 where: p6, Table 10 (p16).
5. Cost.
 number: ~4,000 tokens, ~10 s, $2.00 per 1,000 queries, against Zero-shot-CoT $0.40, MEP $1.60, o1 $12.00 at ~30 s.
 setup: averaged over 100 TruthfulQA queries; costs are estimates.
 quote: "MetaCrit buys comparable reliability at one sixth the cost and one third the latency, while the added cost over Zero-shot-CoT purchases +23.7 points".
 where: p9, Table 8.
6. Ablation on TruthfulQA.
 number: full 94.12; without monitor 75.28; without control 76.62.
 where: Table 1.
7. Gains on other backbones (Table 12).
 number: TruthfulQA 95.83 (GPT-4o), 97.55 (Claude-3.5-Sonnet), 98.77 (Claude-Opus-4.6), 93.83 (GPT-4.1), 93.75 (DeepSeek-v3).
 quote: "on Claude-Opus-4.6 and GPT-4.1, MetaCrit lifts TruthfulQA by +4.48 and +6.07 over zero-shot, whereas MEP regresses below zero-shot (85.19 vs. 94.29; 82.72 vs. 87.76)".
 note: those two zero-shot figures (94.29, 87.76) are not in Table 7.
8. Failure analysis shows what a critique-based pipeline cannot fix (App. G/H).
 number: Of 48 TruthfulQA errors, 27 are "consensus collapse" (56.3%) and 13 are knowledge gap (27.1%). All 8 CIAR failures are reconciliation failures.
 quote: "all agents converge on the same plausible but incorrect answer, leaving the meta-level synthesizer with no conflicting signal to correct."
 where: p21-22, Tables 13-14.
9. Monitor-only flagging is worse than both agents flagging.
 number: TruthfulQA accuracy: both flag 94.12, control only 83.1, monitor only 64.0, neither 73.7.
 quote: "Accuracy drops when the monitoring agent flags alone (64.0%), suggesting that monitoring-only questioning without logical follow-up can destabilise correct answers." See inconsistencies below.
10. Per-instance intervention strength d_i = 1 − cos(R_i, F_i) correlates weakly with raw-answer quality.
 number: Spearman rho −0.23, 95% CI [−0.35, −0.09], n=204. Correlation with monitor departure on TruthfulQA is 0.46, CrowS-Pairs 0.75, MMLU 0.04. The authors call embedding distance "a proxy for critique intensity, not a calibrated measure."
 where: p8, Table 11.
11. Drop-in agents (Table 3).
 number: monitor on Zero-shot-CoT 70.38 to 77.60 TruthfulQA, 24 to 28 CIAR. Control on MEP 89.35 to 94.24 TruthfulQA, 82 to 96 CIAR.
12. User study (n=45, GPT-4o backbone, forced-choice preference among 3 systems).
 number: Critical-thinking preference 41.7% (MA+MetaCrit) vs 26.4% (MA) vs 31.9% (single agent). Instructiveness 39.4 / 28.3 / 32.2. Cronbach's alpha 0.804 and 0.732, but Cohen's kappa 0.293 and 0.304.
 quote: "Interactiveness and Intelligence are unreliable here (α= 0.197, 0.221; p > .05)".
 where: p9, Table 4.
13. Safety is not bought by hedging.
 number: BOLD 776 prompts, HONEST 705 items, both 0.000. Mean output 19.6 words on BOLD, 25.2 on HONEST. Disclaimer language in 0.1% and 0.0% of completions.
 where: App. B.5.
 caveat: those two benchmarks are saturated, with several methods also at 0.000. The authors say the claim is therefore "the joint one".

LIMITS
Stated (p10): "TruthfulQA relies on a GPT-4o judge, CIAR has only 50 items, and safety evaluation is English-only." Training-free baselines on closed-weight models only, so trained ReflectEvo and ReMA are untested. The user study is one institution, homogeneous. Latency is 5x cost and ~10 s. Embedding distance is only a proxy.
Unstated or observed:
- Single run per cell, no seeds or temperature given. Intervals are given only in Table 10.
- GPT-3.5-Turbo is a weak and dated backbone. The gap shrinks on GPT-4o, and the authors say as much.
- Table 1 mixes reproduced numbers (§ from Long et al., † from Liang et al.) with their own re-runs, yet the caption says "All rows share one backbone, items, formats, and scoring." The MEP 89.35 and all of the Zero-shot-CoT, Self-refine, Self-consistency, ExpertPrompting and MAD TruthfulQA numbers are marked §.
- The information-flow analysis uses an n=204 subset (and n=98 to 230 on other datasets) against the full 817 in the headline.
- The raw-critique baseline is one sentence. It tests placement, not critique quality.
- The paper has no agent, tool or trajectory evaluation anywhere.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES (checked against the paper's own tables)
- The CrowS-Pairs ablation is described backwards. The text says removing control "improves accuracy (82.07% vs. 79.08%)", but Table 2 gives full = 82.07 and without-control = 79.08. Removal lowers accuracy. The "deactivate ϕ↓ when the signal is clear" heuristic is therefore not supported by Table 2.
- Table 3 shows MEP + control scoring 94.24 on TruthfulQA and 96 on CIAR, and MEP + monitor 93.15 and 92. Both exceed full MetaCrit on CIAR (84) and the control variant exceeds it on TruthfulQA (94.12). This is not squared with "highest of all twelve baselines".
- Section 5.1 says general models reach "24–60%" on CIAR, but Table 7 lists gpt-4o at 74 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet at 76.
- Table 13: the TruthfulQA rows sum to n=204, not 817. Weighted by those rows the accuracy is about 80%, not 94.12, and the "both flag" row reads 94.12 in the table but 95.12 in the text. CIAR n sums to 12 (not 50), the text says "all four... answered correctly (96%)", and Table 14 shows 8 CIAR failures while Table 13 implies about 3.
- Appendix L.2 preference rates differ from Table 4: Interactiveness MetaCrit 33.9 vs 35.1, multi-agent 31.5 vs 30.4. Intelligence single agent 36.9 vs 37.5.
- In Appendix H, the worked CIAR failure cases have garbled arithmetic. For example, the "distinct natural numbers sum to 100" analysis contradicts itself.
- The survey repeats questions: Q25 duplicates Q22, and Q26-27 duplicate Q23-24.
- The paper says MetaCrit is "preferred" overall. It is preferred only on the two dimensions the authors call reliable, and the single-agent baseline leads on Intelligence in the appendix.
- Version drift: ledger title MCPEval vs actual content (see above).

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Nelson and Narens (1990) metamemory monitoring/control, and Flavell (1979).
- Self-refine (Madaan et al. 2023).
- Multi-Expert Prompting (Long et al. 2024), whose TruthfulQA protocol and reproduced numbers are used.
- Zero-shot-CoT (Kojima et al. 2023).
- Universal Self-consistency (Chen et al. 2023).
- ExpertPrompting (Xu et al. 2023).
- MAD (Liang et al. 2024).
- ReflectEvo (Li et al. 2025), DMC (Wang et al. 2025), Metacognitive Prompting (Wang and Zhao 2024), MGV (Oh 2025), ReMA (Wan et al. 2025), SOFAI-LM (Khandelwal et al. 2025).
- Self-bias: Xu et al. 2024, "Pride and prejudice".
- Debate caveat: Smit et al. 2024.
- Benchmarks: TruthfulQA (Lin et al. 2022), CIAR (Yamin et al. 2025), BOLD, HONEST, CREAK, MMLU, BBQ, CrowS-Pairs.

CODE: none. Prompts are in Appendix C (Figures 5-8, p18) and the algorithm is Algorithm 1 (p3). The monitor prompt is worth quoting if you keep it: "Should or shouldn't there be only one possible and objective answer to this question? In other words, is answer proven by science or facts?"

FIGURES (captions via figures.py)
- Fig 2 (p3): the four-agent pipeline. This is the one to reuse if anything goes in.
- Fig 3 (p7): cumulative similarity change per agent. It shows mid-pipeline dips, but the metric is embedding similarity to the reference, so it is weak evidence.
- No figure shows the result "uniform critique over-corrects". Table 1's raw-critique block does that, and it is a table (p7).
- Fig 4 (p17) is the user-study heatmap. Fig 17 (p21) is the worked zodiac trace.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF text.
- The ledger metadata (MCPEval) is wrong for this PDF. The title, reason and target-note rationale need correcting, and this paper should probably be re-routed or dropped for 06-evaluating-agents.md.
- Extraction is clean apart from garbled table layout (Tables 1, 2 and 13 columns were interleaved and I reassembled them by eye), flattened Figure 3 axis labels, and symbols that came out mangled (ϕ↑/↓, set operators).
- The arXiv v4 date of 27 Sep 2026 is a later revision of a July 2025 submission. The older "2025" in the filename understates how much was revised, and the baselines list contains 2025-2026 methods.
